assertion.statement: For the unbranched rational contact-line point s, the entire principal-level-three D210 fiber has a normal splitting field L/Q with [L:Q] dividing576. Its abelian surfaces and all geometric homomorphisms between them are defined over L, and rad(D_L N_bad) divides B_* M_5(s).
assertion.objects: The entire canonical principal-level-three scheme Y of the maximal quaternion order of discriminant210, its fiber over s, the constant normalizer group Gamma, the actual normal splitting field L, and the universal fiber surfaces with full three-torsion markings.
assertion.hypotheses: The full fine-cover construction, canonical rational normalizer action and five-section contact-line identification are supplied. The selected rational s avoids the branch/contact set. The smooth tame quotient models away from210 and their local equations are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such rational s and every pair of fiber surfaces over the same full fiber splitting field.
assertion.parameter_range: Quaternion discriminant210; level3 is ramified in the quaternion algebra; all arithmetic components of the cover are included.
assertion.uniformity: The degree bound576 and the ramification support bound hold for every permitted s without choosing or adjoining a further field for geometric homomorphisms.
assertion.constants: Degree over stack72, generic coarse degree36; |W|=16; |Gamma|=576; B_*=product of primes at most76176.
assertion.normalizations: Use the whole canonical model and its regular action, not one complex component. The Galois image lies in the regular centralizer. Hom is the integral geometric Hom lattice; congruence modulo3 applies after all fiber3-torsion markings are defined.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No application of a prime-to-discriminant level theorem at3. The height calculation at bad primes uses the maximal stack separately. This does not construct Lprime, normalize the modular representation, or prove a numerical Faltings-height bound.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the whole fine cover and canonical action; choose s; split its finite fiber; descend all Hom using the same L; apply tame local contact equations to the ramification and reduction support.
